To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the serum levels of MMP9 and TIMP1 in patients with non-small-cell lung cancer were significantly higher than those in healthy individuals.
serum concentrations of metalloproteinases (MMP)-2 and -9 were significantly higher in patients with non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC), compared to controls.
the serum concentration of metalo-proteinase 2 and 9 in non-small cell cancer patients is significantly increased in comparison to healthy controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the relationship between the concentration of metalloprotease 9 and the concentration of metalprotease 2 in non-smoking cell lung cancer patients, and the relationship with the degree of the tumor and the degree of the lymph node metastasis.
the study of the serum concentrations of MMP2 and MMP9 in NSCLC patients and their relationship with the clinical and pathological characteristics.
the serum concentration of metaloproteinase 9 and metaloproteinase-2 in non-small-cell lung cancer patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the serum concentrations of metalloproteinases 1 and 2 are not elevated in patients with non-small cell lung cancers.
MMP-9 and MMP-2 are elevated in the sera of non-small cell lung carcinoma patients.
MMP-2 and MMP-9 are not suitable as a biomarker for the detection of NSCLC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the serum concentration of metaloproteinase 2 and 9 is increased in patients with non small cell lung cancer.
the serum concentrations of metalloproteinases 1, 2 and 9 were increased in NSCLC patients.
the serum concentration of matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-2 and MMP-9 are significantly increased in patients with lung cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a novel mechanism for the regulation of MMP9 activity in the lung and have demonstrated that MMP9 is an important mediator of lung fibrosis.
the metalloproteinases (MMP-2 and MMP-9) are involved in the development of non-small cell lung cancers.
there are many ways to improve the accuracy of the diagnosis of lung cancer.
